title: U.S. House · Alaska At-Large
area: Statewide, Alaska's single at-large congressional district.

context.text: Alaska uses a top-four nonpartisan primary followed by ranked-choice voting in the general election. Incumbent Nicholas Begich (R) won the August 18, 2026 primary with 44.6%, followed by Bill Hill (Nonpartisan) with 32.5%. John Brendan Williams (D), who placed fifth, withdrew from the general election; Jim McDermott (L), who finished eighth, replaced him on the ballot.

candidates.name: Nicholas Begich

summary.text: Nicholas Begich is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat. He is a technology entrepreneur who previously founded FarShore Partners and co-founded the investment firm Dashfire.

background.text: Born in Anchorage, Alaska; earned a B.B.A. in entrepreneurship from Baylor University (1999) and an M.B.A. from Indiana University-Bloomington (2002).
Founded FarShore Partners, a technology development company, and co-founded Dashfire, a startup investment firm.
Completed a fellowship with the Club for Growth and co-chaired the Alaska Republican Party's Finance Committee and Rep. Don Young's 2020 re-election campaign.

positions.summary: Voted against a three-year extension of ACA health insurance subsidies, saying an extension does not fix the Affordable Care Act and that he wants reforms to it.
positions.quote: The health insurance system created by Democrats under Obamacare has proven completely unaffordable for the American healthcare customer

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 38, the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2025, a bill allowing nonresidents of a state to carry concealed firearms there if their home state permits it.
Cosponsored H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act, a bill to require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

record.text: Serves on the House Natural Resources Committee (Vice Chair of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee), the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Bill Hill

summary.text: Bill Hill is a nonpartisan candidate who placed second in the August 2026 top-four primary. He is a commercial fisherman, former teacher, and construction worker from Naknek, Alaska, running on affordability, anti-corruption and fisheries issues.

background.text: Grew up in a small village in rural Alaska, hunting, fishing, and raising sled dog teams.
Has worked as a commercial fisherman, school teacher, and construction worker.
Lives in Naknek, Alaska with his wife Diane; describes himself as a father of four and grandfather of seven.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare for Alaskans, citing fuel prices as high as $15 a gallon in some rural communities.
A total ban on congressional stock trading and reducing the influence of money in elections.
Opposing trawl bycatch to protect Alaska fisheries, and investing in schools.

statements.quote: I think everybody should have access to good health care. That's the bottom line.
So, let’s find ways to implement renewable energies.
statements.context: In a KFSK interview in Petersburg, August 2026

statements.quote: Billionaires and corporations need to pay their share like the rest of us. And we need to get big money out of our elections.

candidates.researchNotes: Hill has no campaign site text that could be fetched here; statements come from KMXT and KFSK interviews. His interviews take sides on few of the guide's statements; he describes himself as pro-development and opposes the Pebble Mine (not a guide issue).

candidates.name: Eric Hafner

summary.text: Eric Hafner is the Democratic nominee. He is incarcerated at a federal prison in New York, serving a 20-year sentence for threatening elected officials, with a scheduled release date in 2036.

background.text: At the time of a 2024 Alaska Democratic Party lawsuit seeking to remove him from that year's ballot, Hafner was serving a 20-year federal prison sentence in New York for threatening elected officials, with a scheduled release in 2036.

An Alaska Superior Court judge dismissed the Alaska Democratic Party's 2024 lawsuit to remove Hafner from the ballot; the judge ruled that ranked-choice voting eliminated any claim of harm from his presence on the ballot and that the court could not weigh in on whether he would reside in Alaska by Election Day.

positions.summary: In an Alaska Beacon interview (quoted on Ballotpedia), said healthcare decisions are between a woman and her medical provider and that returning to the 1950s does not work.
positions.quote: Healthcare decisions are between a woman and her medical provider.

positions.summary: Said as a Democrat he supports "Healthcare For All" among traditional Democratic Party positions (Alaska Beacon interview quoted on Ballotpedia).
positions.quote: Healthcare For All including the Right to Choose

positions.summary: In an Alaska Beacon interview (quoted on Ballotpedia), said the oil and gas economy is in transition and called for stabilizing those industries by discontinuing expansion while other income sources are developed.
positions.quote: The world is moving toward a greener approach, away from environmentally damaging fossil fuels.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statement of positions could be located; Hafner has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Ballotpedia's coverage of Hafner focuses on the ballot-eligibility litigation rather than a policy platform.

candidates.name: Jim McDermott

summary.text: Jim McDermott is the Libertarian nominee. He is a business instructor at the University of Alaska and a 22-year veteran of the U.S. Air Force who finished eighth in the August 2026 primary and joined the general-election ballot after a higher-finishing candidate withdrew.

background.text: Holds a B.S. in occupational education from Wayland Baptist University and an M.S. in business organizational management from the University of La Verne.
Served 22 years in the U.S. Air Force and works as a business instructor for the University of Alaska.
Has run for this seat in previous cycles, including 2012, 2014, and 2016.

priorities.text: Term limits: says career politicians surrounded by other career politicians stop thinking clearly about what ordinary Americans need, and that he would not seek a third term.
Fiscal accountability: supports zero-based budgeting and balanced budget requirements at the federal level.
Civil liberties: says the Patriot Act and the NDAA drove him out of the Republican Party and that they should be repealed or fundamentally reformed.

positions.summary: Campaign website says tariffs are paid by American businesses and consumers and calls for no international tariffs or trade barriers.
positions.quote: No international tariffs, no trade barriers, no federal schemes that make Alaskans pay more for the things they need.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he does not support open-ended military commitments made without Congressional authorization.
positions.quote: He does not support open-ended military commitments made without Congressional authorization. The War Powers Resolution exists for a reason.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from the issues page of his campaign website (jamesmcdermott.org), which is written in the third person. He has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His answers to the Alaska newsroom questionnaire were not located.

statements.quote: He opposes treating immigration as primarily a law enforcement issue when the underlying cause is an immigration system that does not function.
